points.text: Context KL term trains on the same forget questions and gold contexts used for contextual evaluation (train-on-test).
No evaluation with other context forms: paraphrased, partial, long, multi-document or noisy RAG retrieval.
No generalization test on different questions or held-out forget examples not used in context term.
Robustness evidence is one hand-picked example with manual paraphrases; anecdotal.
Forgetting may be undermined; not tested under stronger probes, relearning or jailbreak attacks.
'No cost' claim overstated: Direct QA forgetting metrics worsen for RMU and NPO; slack allowed.
Standard TOFU forget quality, truth ratio and probability metrics dropped.
No general-capability benchmark beyond TOFU utility aggregate.
Lambda and epochs selected on evaluation data (oracle selection), no validation split.
No seeds or variance reported.
Insensitivity-to-lambda claim rests only on Gemma curves; chosen values vary widely.
Missing simpler baselines: CE/SFT on gold-context prompts, retain-set augmentation, KL-vs-CE ablation, prompt-only.
Only three of six unlearning methods receive the fix.
All evidence from synthetic TOFU; no transfer to pre-trained knowledge benchmarks like WMDP or MUSE.
No larger models or long multi-fact contexts evaluated.
Motivating examples (outdated regulations, historical comparison) differ substantially from evaluation setting.
Target of original-level contextual QA questionable; retrain-on-retain model's contextual QA not reported.
Binary Claude LLM-Judge not validated against human judgments.
LLM-Judge appears lenient when answer is in prompt (ROUGE vs Judge gap on Qwen).
Qualitative examples are single instances.
Vanilla RMU/GradAscent gibberish suggests general collapse rather than selective context suppression.
Mechanistic claim that suppression ripples through representation space is asserted, not measured.
Vanilla contextual failure may reflect over-training; no early-stopped or lower-LR baselines.
Modest novelty: KL regularizer to original model close to existing retain KL and distillation.
TOFU entities are independent; evaluate on interconnected data (PISTOL) and real pretraining data.
ContextQA appends clean gold answers; should test long, noisy realistic RAG contexts.
Method expands attack surface for prompt extraction; robustness to attacks not evaluated.
Approach conflicts with unlearning safety/compliance requirements, questioning practical deployability.
Knowledge editing more appropriate for outdated knowledge; reuse of forgotten information rarely needed.
Problem better framed as effect of unlearning on in-context learning than knowledge recovery.
Only two small/mid-sized instruction-tuned models evaluated.
Only synthetic TOFU benchmark used, limiting generalizability.
Limited theoretical justification or guarantees for contextual utility preservation.
Retaining knowledge recoverable via context may violate privacy/regulations; context is more an attack than objective.
Robustness to quantization, prompt and extraction attacks not tested.
Missing activation-steering fine-grained unlearning baseline for context suppression.
Fix is a straightforward KL-consistency term akin to RLHF/DPO regularizers; limited technical novelty.
KL to original model inherits its grounding flaws; no alternative anchors or miscalibration analysis.
GradDiff, DPO, GradAscent results missing from Table 2.

P.summary: Context term trained on the evaluation questions and contexts
No evaluation with other/noisy/realistic context forms
No held-out questions or forget examples for generalization
Forgetting robustness under attacks/probes not tested
No-cost claim overstated; Direct QA worsens
Lambda insensitivity claim only on Gemma
Fix applied to only three of six methods
Only synthetic TOFU; no real pre-trained knowledge benchmarks

Q.summary: Only synthetic TOFU; need interconnected/real data
Clean context; need realistic noisy RAG contexts
Recoverable knowledge conflicts with privacy/compliance goals
Weak motivation: editing more appropriate, reuse rare
Problem framing should be unlearning vs in-context learning
KL anchor inherits original model flaws
